title: Gravitational potential and energy; Power and efficiency
source: Questions copied unchanged from the mission-lesson scripts for AP Physics C: Mechanics (status of the source: mission-lesson scripts of Oct-Nov 2026 (reviewed by AI reviewers; not signed off by a person)). Terms and clues: E03-1#t1 term and clue written for the game; E03-1#t2 term and clue written for the game; C04-2#t1 term and clue written for the game; C04-2#t2 term and clue written for the game. Questions: C04-2#N.2, E03-1#N.14, C04-2#N.4, E03-1#N.15, C04-2#N.6a.

assemble.prompt: Match each term to its definition.

items.label: Power
items.clue: Rate of doing work, or rate of energy transfer.

items.label: Watt
items.clue: Unit equal to one joule transferred each second.

items.label: Escape speed
items.clue: Minimum launch value of v that lets an object just reach infinity.

items.label: Total energy
items.clue: Sum K + U, which must be at least zero for an object to reach infinity.

questions.stem: A satellite in a circular orbit of radius r around a planet has kinetic energy K₀. The satellite is moved to a circular orbit of radius 4r around the same planet. What is its kinetic energy in the new orbit?

A cart starts from rest on a level track with negligible friction. A constant horizontal force is exerted on the cart, and no other horizontal force acts on it. At time t after the cart starts, the power delivered to the cart by the force is P. The power delivered by the force at time 2t is how many times P?

A probe is launched straight up from the surface of a planet with exactly the escape speed. The planet has no atmosphere, its motion is negligible, and the only force exerted on the probe after launch is the planet's gravitational force. Which statement describes the probe's motion after launch?

options.text: It slows down until it is beyond the reach of gravity, then moves at a constant speed.
It slows to a stop at a large but finite distance, then falls back to the planet.
It slows down all the time, its speed approaching zero as its distance approaches infinity.
It speeds up as it moves away, since U_g decreases as its distance increases.

questions.stem: Motor A raises a 200 N load through 3.0 m in 6.0 s. Motor B raises a 100 N load through 6.0 m in 4.0 s. Both lift at constant speed. Which statement is correct?

options.text: A develops more power, as it lifts the heavier load.
B does more work, as it lifts its load twice as high.
Both do equal work, and B develops more power.
Both develop equal power, as they do equal work.

questions.explanation: Each does 600 J (200 × 3.0 and 100 × 6.0). B does it in less time: 600 ÷ 4.0 = 150 W against 600 ÷ 6.0 = 100 W.

questions.stem: The escape speed from the surface of planet X is v₀. Planet Y has the same mass as planet X but four times its radius. What is the escape speed from the surface of planet Y?
